question: Should the repo execute a full preserved-subset move, a narrower pilot, or stop with a design-ready no-op?

decision.summary: The preserved old GC redirect family should not move as one full subset. A representative ISS-first pilot is now the defended next execution lane, while GC-PRB-0001 stays deferred.
decision.recommendedNextSlice: Open one bounded execution slice for a representative ISS legacy-redirect relocation pilot.

immediateHandling: Keep the old root path occupied by a root stub rather than deleting the historical landing surface.
Move only the retained full body for the pilot record to docs/governance/contracts/support-only/<same-basename>.md.
Add the moved full body to docs/governance/contracts/support-only/INDEX.md.
Rewrite only bounded direct full-body references; lineage and old-ID landing references may continue to cite the root stub path.
whyNow: The ISS family already shares a uniform single-successor redirect model.
Its root-path references are concentrated in lineage and cleanup-boundary surfaces that remain compatible with a stub-preserved root path.
A one-record pilot can prove the move checklist without forcing a five-record wave immediately.

immediateHandling: Keep the full retained redirect body at docs/governance/contracts/ for now.
Do not fold PRB into the first ISS execution packet.
Revisit only in a separate umbrella-specific slice that judges the umbrella redirect together with its already-moved support-only backfill relationship.
whyNotNow: PRB remains a multi-successor umbrella redirect rather than a simple single-successor record.
PRB still carries stronger canonical deprecated-sample weight in earlier registry-model surfaces.
The umbrella-plus-backfill pairing deserves an explicit execution judgment rather than inheriting the ISS pilot decision.
